title: Mixtures and Separation
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Mixtures and Separation Worksheets (Filtration, Distillation, Chromatography)
standard_code: KS3 Chemistry: Pure and impure substances
standard_text: The concept of a pure substance; mixtures, including dissolving; diffusion in terms of the particle model; simple techniques for separating mixtures: filtration, evaporation, distillation and chromatography; the identification of pure substances.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on mixtures and separation: pure substances, dissolving, filtration, evaporation, distillation, chromatography and melting points. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Different properties let us separate mixtures.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mixtures can be separated because their substances have different properties.

  • Filtration: insoluble solid from a liquid. Evaporation: dissolved solid from a solution. Distillation: a liquid from a solution or two liquids.
  • Chromatography separates dyes. A pure substance gives one spot and has a sharp melting point.
  • When a solute dissolves in a solvent, mass is conserved.
Example

Sand and water?

Sand is insoluble

Answer: filtration

Example

10 g salt + 100 g water. Mass of solution?

Mass is conserved

Answer: 110 g

Common mistakes

  • Thinking salt disappears when it dissolves.
  • Thinking filtering salt water removes the salt.
  • Thinking pure means natural.

faq.a: In science, a pure substance is a single element or compound with nothing else mixed in. It melts and boils at fixed temperatures.
